chapter: Cotton Club and radio fame with Cab
title: Radio airtime from the Duke Ellington break
summary: The Cotton Club broadcasts on CBS and NBC made the band; Thomas wanders into network ownership before Hinton steers back to music.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working radio and television: network shows, studio staffs, talk-show bands

blocks.x: Tell me what the reaction was.

That break we got with Duke made us, because we got on the air. And in them days, the air-time was it. We was on CBS... I still think... I shouldn't make this remark. But I still think there's some connection between NBC and NBC. See, we had... When we was on NBC, if we couldn't get on NBC, they'd put us on WEAF(?). We had that alternate thing, we could go on one... And they had the same line in there...
Well, that was a subsidiary of NBC.
And to this day, I see how close ABC and NBC is.
They're right across the street from one another.
Yeah, but ABC and NBC do more swapping than any... Where did they put Barbara Walters? They got rid of Barbara Walters...
Well, that's not what we're into anyway.
No. Right. And we had so many guys that were... I'll tell you another guy that used to be an announcer, the baseball announcer, the Yankee guy... I remember he was from St. Louis, you know.
But we're not into the sports now. We're into the music thing.
